claim: Calibration is a conditional property relative to an information level: the expected proper loss of an A-measurable predictor splits into a proper-regret (reliability) term and a conditional-entropy (residual uncertainty) term, with a chain decomposition for nested levels A subset B.
stance_target: F: calibration is relative to an information level (instrument-conditional)
quoted_support: Calibration is a conditional property that depends on the information retained by a predictor. We develop decomposition identities for arbitrary proper losses that make this dependence explicit.

scope_conditions: Sec 3, Prop 3.2 (calibration error as proper regret)
quoted_support: this yields a three-term identity: miscalibration, a grouping term measuring information loss from X to S, and irreducible uncertainty at the feature level.

claim: Perfect calibration is defined as P(Y in . | S) = S almost surely, equivalently C = S, and post-hoc recalibration cannot recover information already lost in the compression X to S.
stance_target: recalibration changes reliability but not grouping term
quoted_support: Even if one post-processes S to make it calibrated, the compression X ↦ S can cause unavoidable information loss
